sourceInformation.tech: JavaScript, Canvas 2D, my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (8ecc2f6), AI Hub client 1.4.0 (35a1047)
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original shaded pixel toy theatre; plum floor, luminous violet walls, expressive cool-coloured heroes
sourceInformation.animation: Native Blob squash, look and footfall with original antennae, mouths, tells, turn anticipation and event effects
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-generated chip score, SFX and formant gibberish voices; music defaults to 10%; human listening quality unknown
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo/couch co-op; AI Hub 1–2-seat host-authoritative shared-world campaign, including dedicated host
sourceInformation.testing: Headless deterministic simulation, legal-intent playthroughs, browser/controller/touch stand-ins and official Hub harness; no FPS target
sourceInformation.research: Original manual, contemporary audiovisual observations, archival commercial contact sheet, pinned engine and Hub source

testingFeedback: 9 unique game issues were found and fixed; test-fixture corrections were counted separately.
Legal-intent full campaigns and the dedicated-host latency/loss run, combined with the pen shortcut measurement.
Syntax-only checks: useful for parsing, but they cannot establish maze readability, interception or controller feel.
engineFeedback: Native shaded pixels, Blob squash/look/feet, procedural sound buses and the TV Shell gave the game a consistent base.
Yes. I initially made the outer pen detour too short and rearmed an attract transition each input tick; route and runtime tests corrected both.
The authoritative graph, moving-snack simulation, swept contacts, validated workshop and host-authoritative Hub adapter.
Extending grid motion for expiring turns, immediate reversal and tunnel seams while keeping rendering and networking separate from the rules.
No vendored engine changes. GraphMover subclasses the native mover; original art, mouth/antenna animation, UI and synthesis extend native systems.
An official GridMover graph-edge adapter with tunnel transforms, expiring buffers and swept motion segments.
promptFeedback: The distinctive moving-food premise and concrete acceptance checks for a complete playable game.
The first-player duration is a hypothesis; strong route-planning bots finish much faster, and human first-run timing is unknown.
Keeping six stages, the editor, couch co-op, dedicated hosting, touch and final-file packaging consistent under one ruleset.
Separate mandatory feature gates from pacing hypotheses and request measured timing ranges rather than an assumed first-run duration.

aiHub.name: K.C. Munchkin Mix-Up
aiHub.description: Hunt twelve runaway snacks while three hungry rivals hunt you. Ride a turning pen, cut through side doors, reveal shy walls, and build your own mischievous mazes.
aiHub.controls: WASD/arrows or stick/D-pad: move; Space/Cross: reveal; Escape/Options: menu. Couch duo: WASD+F / arrows+period.
